name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
summary: Commercial Linux distribution certified for enterprise servers and critical production environments, offering a guaranteed 10-year lifecycle, SELinux hardening and Podman container management.
license: Open Source (GNU GPL, LGPL and various free licences with a commercial Red Hat assistance and certification subscription)

content.introduction: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) is a commercial Linux distribution developed by Red Hat (a subsidiary of IBM since 2019). RHEL is the reference enterprise operating platform on the global market of data centres, cloud infrastructures, the banking sector, telecommunications and public services. Designed to guarantee maximum reliability, security and operational predictability, RHEL stands out through a rigorous engineering process combining a stabilised Linux kernel, extensive hardware and software certifications and multi-year lifecycle policies.
content.what_is_it: Technically, RHEL is a complete Linux distribution articulated around the systemd system manager, the RPM packaging format and the DNF dependency manager. It is essential to distinguish RHEL from the other projects of its ecosystem: Fedora constitutes its fast-innovation upstream laboratory; CentOS Stream serves as the continuous development (midstream) branch prefiguring the future minor versions of RHEL; while RHEL is the certified, hardened commercial product accompanied by service level agreements (SLA). Compatible distributions built downstream (downstream rebuilds) such as AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux strive to reproduce its binary compatibility without commercial affiliation with Red Hat.
content.kernel_stability_backporting_and_appstre: The RHEL kernel rests on a strict stabilisation policy: rather than continuously adopting the major upstream versions of the Linux kernel, Red Hat maintains a proven base version and applies thousands of backports of critical security fixes and recent hardware drivers to it, thus preserving the integrity of the kernel binary interface (kABI). To reconcile this durability of the foundation with the need to use recent development tools, RHEL implements **Application Streams** (AppStream): this mechanism makes it possible to deploy several competing and independent versions of languages, web servers or databases (Python, Node.js, PHP, PostgreSQL) without affecting the central libraries of the operating system.
content.enterprise_security_architecture_and_sel: RHEL security is articulated around **SELinux** (Security-Enhanced Linux), enabled and applied by default in strict mode (enforcing) with targeted policies that confine daemons and network services in restricted domains to curb compromises. The system also integrates system-wide encryption policies (**System-wide Crypto Policies**), allowing administrators to switch all cryptographic protocols (TLS, SSH, IPsec, Kerberos) to strict regulatory compliance levels (FIPS 140-3, PCI-DSS). Added to these are centralised identity management (Red Hat IdM based on FreeIPA) and the OpenSCAP automated auditing suite.
content.containers_virtualization_and_cockpit_ma: For modern application workloads, RHEL promotes a daemonless and unprivileged container ecosystem, relying on native tools compliant with OCI standards: **Podman** (container and pod management), **Buildah** (image building) and **Skopeo** (container image handling). For enterprise virtualisation, RHEL integrates the native **KVM** hypervisor driven by **libvirt**. Local and remote administration is facilitated by the **Cockpit** web console, offering a refined and secure graphical interface to supervise processor resources, XFS/Stratis volume storage, network interfaces and service logs.
content.lifecycle_policies_and_hardware_platform: The official lifecycle policy of Red Hat guarantees a lifetime of **10 years** for each major version of RHEL, split into a full support phase (Full Support Phase of 5 years, with driver additions and major fixes) and a maintenance phase (Maintenance Support Phase of 5 years, dedicated to critical security fixes), completed by paid extended support options (Extended Life Phase - ELP / EUS). RHEL is certified and optimised for four enterprise hardware architectures: **x86-64**, **AArch64** (64-bit ARM), **IBM POWER** (ppc64le) and **IBM Z** mainframes (s390x).
advantages: Reference enterprise stability and reliability with durable kABI and rigorous backports.
Standard 10-year lifecycle guaranteed per major version with extended support options (EUS/ELP).
Hardened security by default with SELinux in enforcing mode and system cryptographic policies.
Application Streams mechanism making it possible to evolve development tools without touching the foundation.
Modern and secure daemonless container ecosystem (Podman, Buildah, Skopeo).
Extensive worldwide hardware and regulatory certifications (FIPS 140-3, Common Criteria, OEM manufacturer support).
disadvantages: Commercial model under paid subscription for access to certified binaries and official technical support.
Deliberately slow pace of evolution of the system foundation software compared with fast community distributions.
Access to source repositories subject to the contractual terms of the Red Hat customer portal.
Complexity of configuring advanced SELinux security policies for administrators not familiar with them.
Less suited to personal desktop computers or to video game-oriented workstations.
who_is_it_for: Large enterprises, banks, ministries and telecommunications operators requiring contractual 24/7 support.
System administrators managing fleets of critical physical servers or hybrid cloud clusters.
Infrastructure architects designing container platforms based on Red Hat OpenShift.
Developers certifying enterprise software for industrial production environments.
who_is_it_not_for: Private users looking for a free desktop distribution for their everyday laptop.
Developers immediately requiring the very latest graphics drivers or the latest daily package versions.
Players of recent PC video games looking for leading-edge gaming performance optimisations.
Small structures or hobby projects without a budget for enterprise commercial support subscriptions.
content.verdict: Red Hat Enterprise Linux is an enterprise Linux distribution published by Red Hat. By guaranteeing ten years of operational continuity, security mechanisms (SELinux, FIPS) and a suite of tools (Podman, Cockpit, AppStream) certified on the x86-64, ARM64, POWER and s390x architectures, it targets critical computing infrastructures.
